what: Surface-Adjusted Elo Ratings for Professional Tennis
title: Surface-Adjusted Elo Ratings for Professional Tennis
text: R package surface-adjusted Elo ratings professional tennis. core functions calculate probability one player beats another update players’ ratings match. Surface-specific ratings (hard, clay, grass) built Jeff Sackmann’s ATP match data development.

title: Surface-Adjusted Elo Ratings for Professional Tennis
Surface-Adjusted Elo Ratings for Professional Tennis
code: library(MSDS457TennisElo)  # Probability a 1700-rated player beats a 1500-rated player elo_expected(1700, 1500) #> [1] 0.7597469  # A 1400-rated player upsets a 1600-rated player elo_update(1400, 1600) #> $winner #> [1] 1424.312 #> #> $loser #> [1] 1575.688

what: Expected win probability from two Elo ratings — elo_expected
title: Expected win probability from two Elo ratings — elo_expected
text: Calculates probability player beats player B, based gap Elo ratings, using standard logistic Elo formula \(E_A = 1 / (1 + 10^{(R_B - R_A) / scale})\). 0-point gap gives 0.5; player rated 200 points higher wins 76% time.

title: Expected win probability from two Elo ratings — elo_expected
Expected win probability from two Elo ratings — elo_expected
text: rating_a Numeric. Elo rating(s) player . rating_b Numeric. Elo rating(s) player B. Must length rating_a, length 1. scale Numeric. Rating gap produces 10--1 odds. Defaults 400, standard chess value.

title: Expected win probability from two Elo ratings — elo_expected
Expected win probability from two Elo ratings — elo_expected
code: # Equal ratings give a 50% chance elo_expected(1500, 1500) #> [1] 0.5  # A 200-point favorite wins about 76% of the time elo_expected(1700, 1500) #> [1] 0.7597469  # Vectorized over several matchups elo_expected(c(1600, 1800, 2000), 1700) #> [1] 0.3599350 0.6400650 0.8490204

what: Update Elo ratings after a match — elo_update
title: Update Elo ratings after a match — elo_update
text: Updates players' ratings single match. winner gains rating points loser drops amount, scaled K-factor surprising result . Inputs follow winner/loser layout ATP match data.

title: Update Elo ratings after a match — elo_update
Update Elo ratings after a match — elo_update
text: winner_rating Numeric. Rating(s) match winner match. loser_rating Numeric. Rating(s) match loser match. k Numeric. K-factor, maximum number points single match can move rating. Defaults 32. scale Numeric. Rating gap produces 10--1 odds. Defaults 400, standard chess value.

title: Update Elo ratings after a match — elo_update
text: list elements winner loser holding updated ratings.

title: Update Elo ratings after a match — elo_update
code: # Two equal players: the winner gains 16 points elo_update(1500, 1500) #> $winner #> [1] 1516 #>  #> $loser #> [1] 1484 #>   # An upset moves more points than an expected result elo_update(1400, 1600) #> $winner #> [1] 1424.312 #>  #> $loser #> [1] 1575.688 #>   # A smaller K-factor makes ratings move more slowly elo_update(1400, 1600, k = 16) #> $winner #> [1] 1412.156 #>  #> $loser #> [1] 1587.844 #>
